# Messages (C4.5): display-message on the status line, at the moment it shows and after it
# goes. The pane runs `exec cat`, never an interactive shell.
conf messages.conf
size 60x10
run new-session -d -s a -n w 'exec cat'
client c 60x10
# Until a key: the message replaces the status line and the cursor is hidden.
run display-message -d 0 hello
screen c
# A key clears it, and goes on to the pane.
type c x
screen c
# Styles in the message, and a format.
run display-message -d 0 '#[fg=red]styled #{session_name} ##'
screen c
# message-style with a width and an alignment.
run set -g message-style 'bg=blue,fg=white,width=20,align=centre' ; display-message -d 0 centred
screen c
run set -gu message-style ; display-message -d 3000 timed
screen c
# -d 1 is gone at once.
run display-message -d 1 gone
screen c
# -N: keys do not clear it, and are dropped.
run display-message -N -d 5000 sticky
type c y
screen c
run display-message -d 1 clear
screen c
# The panes are frozen while a message shows, unless -C.
run display-message -d 0 frozen ; send-keys -t %0 abc
screen c
type c z
screen c
run display-message -C -d 0 unfrozen ; send-keys -t %0 def
screen c
type c w
screen c
# A key binding's error, its first letter capitalised.
run bind -n F2 select-pane -t nope
type c '\x1bOQ'
screen c
type c v
# Without a status line the message takes the last line; with two, message-line chooses.
run set -g status off ; display-message -d 0 'no status'
screen c
type c u
run set -g status 2 ; set -g message-line 1 ; display-message -d 0 'line one'
screen c
type c t
run set -g status-position top ; display-message -d 0 'at the top'
screen c
run kill-server
